headline: Refining margin windfall triples profit; dividend raised
summary_short: HF Sinclair earned $892.0M ($4.93 diluted EPS) in Q2 2026, up 37.7% q/q and more than quadrupling y/y from $208M, as refining margins widened sharply and the board raised the quarterly dividend 5% to $0.525/share.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $10.39B (+45.9% q/q, +53.1% y/y) as adjusted refinery gross margin per barrel jumped 57% y/y to $25.95 on tight Mid-Continent and West Coast crack spreads, despite planned turnarounds at Parco and Navajo and unplanned downtime at El Dorado. Net income reached $892.0M ($4.93 diluted EPS), up 37.7% q/q. Cash rose to $2.26B (+97.0% q/q) after $1.97B of six-month operating cash flow; the company repurchased $251M of stock and paid $180M in dividends YTD. The board raised the quarterly dividend 5% to $0.525/share and expects to run 590,000-620,000 bpd of crude in Q3 2026 given the planned El Dorado turnaround. HF Sinclair also announced plans to separate its Lubricants & Specialties segment.

drivers.explanation: Refining segment saw strong margins and volumes in the Mid-Continent and West regions on steady demand, tight supply and favorable crack spreads, per the release.
Adjusted refinery gross margin per barrel jumped 57% y/y to $25.95, the release's stated primary driver of the revenue and margin increase.
Wider refining margins were partially offset by planned maintenance at Parco and Navajo and unplanned maintenance at El Dorado, per the release.
Tracks the operating income improvement; the effective tax rate rose to 23.9% from 14.5% y/y on state/local taxes, partly offset by renewable-fuel tax benefits, per the filing.
EPS growth slightly outpaced net income growth because diluted share count fell to 179.4M from 188.1M a year ago following buybacks, per the share reconciliation.
Cash build reflects $1.97B of six-month operating cash flow, driven by higher net income and a $668M favorable working-capital swing, per the filing.
Long-term debt was essentially unchanged q/q; not explained in the release beyond routine financing activity.
Equity growth reflects retained net income partially offset by $180M of dividends and $251M of buybacks during the six months, per the equity and cash-flow statements.
